hints.title: Write the two transformations in their stated order
hints.body: Reflecting first gives f(−x). Translating this left by two replaces every x in that expression by x+2, giving g(x)=f(−x−2).
hints.recap: Apply a horizontal operation to the whole current input expression.
hints.pitfall: A left translation replaces x by x+2; the minus sign already inside must distribute over the bracket.
hints.pause: Find h by performing the left translation first and the reflection second.

recall.reminder: Apply a horizontal operation to the whole current input expression.

hints.title: Compare the resulting input expressions
hints.body: For the other order, begin by translating the original function. Apply the reflection to that new input expression. Only then set the two final functions equal.
hints.recap: The order of reflection and translation can change the resulting function.
hints.pitfall: Reflecting x changes x to −x, not the added constant two to negative two.
hints.pause: Derive the second transformed expression and compare its input with the first.

recall.reminder: The order of reflection and translation can change the resulting function.

hints.title: Rename the first input
hints.body: Introduce <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> in your equality of transformed functions, and rewrite the other input entirely in terms of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: A substitution covering all real inputs preserves a universal identity.
hints.pitfall: A repeating shift need not be the smallest positive period.
hints.pause: Find the resulting identity and check that reversing the substitution proves sufficiency.

recall.reminder: A substitution covering all real inputs preserves a universal identity.

solution:
1. Apply the operations in order. Reflection then left translation gives g(x)=f(−(x+2))=f(−x−2). Left translation then reflection gives h(x)=f(−x+2).

2. Equate the functions. They are identical precisely when f(−x−2)=f(−x+2) for every real x.

3. Rename the input. With u=−x−2, this is exactly f(u)=f(u+4) for every real u. Reversing the substitution also proves sufficiency.

Answer B. A smaller period may also exist; the required identity is repetition after four.
knowledgePattern: Compare noncommuting transformations and derive a period identity
